citation.text: Q4 2026E VEVYE holds the latest quarterly TRx sequential rate of about 17% and applies a +10% sequential net price/mix (NPP) residual, calibrated between a tighter year-over-year gap close and a sharp post-NPP cliff. TRx from Q3 2025 onward is reconstructed, not independently measured units, and the revenue/TRx ratio is not a true ASP.

FY2027E VEVYE $255 million and FY2028E $326 million are retained starting assumptions from the prior product build, not a user-chosen override of the rates. The $255 million applies 45% TRx growth to the full FY2026E year, not to a Q3-annualized starting point. Before the Q4 rounding used on the official line (51.133 to 51.1), FY2026E VEVYE is about $141.166 million. Reconstructed FY2026E TRx is 238,338 + 288,389 + 337,415 + (337,415 × 1.17) = 1,258,917.55. That implies a derived full-year net realization of about $112.13 per TRx and a Q4 exit realization of about $129.52 ($51.133 million / 394,775.55), so the Q4 exit is about 15.5% above the FY2026E average (129.52 / 112.13 ≈ 1.155). FY2027E then uses about 1,825,430 TRx (FY2026E TRx × 1.45) at about $139.89 per TRx (Q4 exit × 1.08), or 141.166 × 1.45 × 1.155 × 1.08 ≈ $255.3 million, rounded to the retained $255 million. The residual of about $0.3 million is rounding of that retained assumption, not an unexplained coverage plug. The 8% is the step-up from the Q4 exit; full-year FY2027E derived net price versus the FY2026E average is about 24.7%, not 8%. Revenue/TRx is a derived ratio, not a measured ASP, and TRx from Q3 2025 onward is reconstructed, not independently measured. FY2028E $326 million is not 255 × 1.25 × 1.02 = 325.125 rounded up. It equals $255 million × about 25.3% volume growth × 2% net price (326 / (255 × 1.02) − 1 = 25.336%). A plain 25% volume × 2% NPP on $255 million would be $325.1 million; the retained $326 million traces to an earlier rounded $255.5 million starting point in the prior build and is kept as approximately 25.3% volume and 2% NPP. FY2029E onward is a maturing franchise (about 18%, 14%, 12%, 10% revenue growth) with NPP roughly flat. Composition-patent expiry from December 2030 is a later-window risk; other listed claims run into 2037–2039.

FY2027E TRIESENCE $67.5 million and FY2028E $86.4 million are retained starting assumptions at a constant $535 realization (revenue per customer unit, not a true ASP). That implies about 126,200 units in FY2027E and about 161,500 units in FY2028E. FY2026E units are about 72,000 (9,934 + 14,603 + 20,022 + Q4 at the held +37.1% sequential rate). FY2027E is therefore a continued ramp year of about 75% unit growth from a still-low base, not a mature 21% grower, and FY2028E is about 28% unit growth. U.S. Orange Book patents are listed through 2029. The base lets units keep growing modestly into FY2029E (about 185,800 units, $99.4 million) then flatten in FY2030E–FY2031E and decline about 3% in FY2032E. The next-generation H-N08 pre-filled syringe is expected H2 2028 / H1 2029 but is unapproved and is not in the base as a replacement product.

Volume × net price: 60,000 / 200,000 / 300,000 / 400,000 / 500,000 units in FY2028E–FY2032E at $175 / $180 / $185 / $190 / $195 net realization, or $10.5 / $36.0 / $55.5 / $76.0 / $97.5 million. Base YOCHIL (MELT-210) revenue is an unweighted, conditional path on the company’s expected 2028 timing. End-of-Phase 2 was completed in the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (letter dated 10 August 2026); Phase 3 is still ahead and there is no NDA in 2026, so a 2028 launch is tighter than G-MELT’s. Units = penetration × (1/3) × that year’s IHEEZO customer units, with the same penetration fractions as the G-MELT ramp (60/750, 1/3, 2/3, 1, 1), reaching full capture of that one-third in FY2031E and then tracking IHEEZO. The official IHEEZO unit identity is used (FY28 327,457, then +41,804 a year). Assumed net price follows the G-MELT $175–$195 path; no YOCHIL price is disclosed. YOCHIL is not placed on the cataract 15% target, and G-MELT is not given the IHEEZO third. Compounded MKO remains in ImprimisRx and is not double-counted. The broader diagnostic, endoscopic and anesthesia-induction market is upside and is not in the base. No YOCHIL revenue in this period.

End-of-Phase 2 was completed in the quarter ended 30 June 2026 (letter dated 10 August 2026); Phase 3 is still ahead and there is no NDA in 2026, so a 2028 launch is tighter than G-MELT’s. Units = penetration × (1/3) × that year’s IHEEZO customer units, with the same penetration fractions as the G-MELT ramp (60/750, 1/3, 2/3, 1, 1), reaching full capture of that one-third in FY2031E and then tracking IHEEZO. The official IHEEZO unit identity is used (FY28 327,457, then +41,804 a year). Assumed net price follows the G-MELT $175–$195 path; no YOCHIL price is disclosed. YOCHIL is not placed on the cataract 15% target, and G-MELT is not given the IHEEZO third. Compounded MKO remains in ImprimisRx and is not double-counted. The broader diagnostic, endoscopic and anesthesia-induction market is upside and is not in the base. No YOCHIL revenue in this period.

Q4 2026E cash operating expenses of $68.258 million start from Q3 cash opex of $59.258 million plus a $5.0 million partial-quarter TYRVAYA opex allowance and a $4.0 million allowance for the G-MELT FDA application fee and other submission costs (the company did not quantify the fee separately). Forward G-MELT program spend and the core opex bridge are in S17 and S20.

Q4 2026E GAAP gross margin 75.5% is near the Q3 75% consolidated rate, with better branded mix partly offset by TYRVAYA inventory step-up and the unnamed royalty tier. An inventory step-up of $2.5 million is assumed to hit GAAP (and Adjusted) gross profit and is not added back, because the Company’s Adjusted EBITDA definition does not list inventory step-up as an add-back.

Melt contingent amounts are not deducted from Adjusted EBITDA. The $87,167,940 FDA-approval cash would be a cash outflow within 75 days of achievement, possibly around late 2027 or early 2028 if PDUFA is Q4 2027, and is recorded only as contingent M&A cash, not an expense. The CMS pass-through-and-J-code milestone is $47,942,367 of stock at a contractual $43.13 per share, or about 1,111,578 fixed shares, not cash and not marked to market; it is not assumed to be issued in a specific year because pass-through award is uncertain. Commercial Net Sales milestones are each payable once, can stack in the same year, and are due within 75 days after year-end if Annual Net Sales of Melt Products (including royalties and profit distributions) hit the thresholds on or before December 31, 2035. Combined base G-MELT and YOCHIL sales first exceed $100 of Annual Net Sales in FY2030E, so the first commercial cash milestone is on the base cash_share_adjustments schedule at 31 December 2030; the path does not reach $250 in the explicit window. A second FDA-approval cash payment is not added for YOCHIL.

The conversion is not assumed to be one-for-one or complete; compounded MKO remains in ImprimisRx. Legacy products inside Other branded are the residual after TYRVAYA, BYOOVIZ, OPUVIZ and BYQLOVI and are roughly $23–25.5 million a year. See drivers.csv for the component add-up each year.

Mark L. Baum is a founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer. In 2011 he led the restructuring and reorganization of the Company, was appointed a director in December 2011, CEO in April 2012, and Chairman again from August 2021. He is a graduate, cum laude, of The University of Texas at Arlington and a graduate of California Western School of Law. In 1999 he founded YesRx, an HIV-focused pharmacy business. 5M+ annual U.S. cataract surgeries — G-MELT’s initial target market. 100M+ potential short-duration procedures in several large markets. Path to launch: pre-NDA meeting completed Q4 2026; NDA submission expected November/December 2026; potential FDA approval Q4 2027; potential launch 2028. If FDA-approved, G-MELT could be the only on-label product for sedation during cataract surgery. Exclusive license from Catalent; Zydis® has supported 35+ FDA-approved products.

Durable Growth: A New Product Every Year. At least one new product every year through the end of the decade, launched within Harrow’s existing cost structure and commercial footprint. 2028 pipeline: YOCHIL expected 2028; G-MELT expected 2028.

Surgical serves cataract and refractive surgeons... with G-MELT expected to expand that offering upon FDA approval. We continue to believe the sublingually administered non-opioid G-MELT, if approved for marketing, represents a near-term opportunity to be the only on-label product for sedation during cataract surgery, potentially helping millions of Americans avoid exposure to opioids and IVs during the most common surgical intervention in the United States.

Commercial Readiness and Launch (H2 2028, as then planned): Leverage Harrow’s existing commercial infrastructure and MKO Melt customer network to execute launch preparations — including manufacturing scale-up, packaging, supply-chain validation, reimbursement, market-access planning, and much more. The November 2026 deck subsequently accelerated approval to Q4 2027 and kept launch in 2028.

Our ImprimisRx brand has dispensed over 400,000 compounded MKO Melt troches which, as a compounded formulation, is similar to the MELT-300 product candidate. Customers seem to love the MKO Melt – so much so that they pay for it out of their capitated cataract surgery procedure fees.

Built for Operating Leverage: a scalable cost structure positions Harrow to grow revenue faster than operating expenses over time. Existing infrastructure. 3x Surgical team. Four focused selling teams; G-MELT and YOCHIL sit with the Surgical team.

Base G-MELT revenue is an unweighted, conditional path: it uses the company’s planned 2028 launch, which is itself conditional on approval, and does not assert that the NDA has been or will be approved. First shipments are assumed in mid-2028 (about two commercial quarters) after a Q4 2027 standard-review PDUFA. Volume × net price: 60,000 / 250,000 / 500,000 / 750,000 / 750,000 units in FY2028E–FY2032E at $175 / $180 / $185 / $190 / $195 net realization, or $10.5 / $45.0 / $92.5 / $142.5 / $146.25. The mature unit rate of 750,000 from FY2031E is 15% of the 5 million U.S. cataract surgeries used as the floor of the company’s 5 million-plus initial target, per the 11 November 2026 instruction that an FDA-approved product should exceed a 10% compounded reference; a 10% current annual MKO share is not a verified printed figure in the sources used (printed figures are cumulative troches or cumulative surgeries, plus an 800-institution early-adopter base). Net price is a mid assumption between bundled/capitated facility economics and a possible later separate-reimbursement outcome; pass-through and J-code are not assumed as a base-case certainty. The 100 million-plus short-duration procedure opportunity is upside and is not in the base.

The Catalent Zydis royalty payable by Harrow is not disclosed. Third-party Zydis licenses have been described as a single-digit royalty on net sales (exact rates redacted). The base uses a 7% royalty equivalent plus about 15% manufacturing/COGS and 6% residual distribution, for a 72% G-MELT product gross margin (band 65–78%). The royalty is not assumed to be zero.

G-MELT launch spend is not disclosed. Missing guidance is not treated as zero cost. The base books an explicit program: $12 million pre-launch in FY2027E (manufacturing scale-up, reimbursement, medical, remaining regulatory), $20 million in the FY2028E launch year, and $16–19 million in-market in FY2029E–FY2032E. Bands are roughly ±40%. This is incremental to the existing Surgical team, which the company says will carry G-MELT upon approval and launch within the existing commercial footprint. It does not invent a second 100-person sales force, and it does not double-count the Q3 2026 cash-opex run rate that already includes the 2026 commercial expansion (OSD more than doubled; surgical team 3x).

Central assumption: Harrow records gross product sales and pays Samsung 40% of U.S. net sales, with about 8% other product cost, for a 52% BYOOVIZ/OPUVIZ product gross margin. The rate is not disclosed; the band is a 30% share (about 62% product GM) to a 50% share (about 42% product GM). An alternative presentation in which Harrow recognizes only its retained share as revenue would lower reported revenue and raise the reported margin percentage, with a similar dollar gross profit if the share is the same rate. The base does not use the 30% or 50% rate and does not net the share from revenue.

Product gross margins before amortization used in the weighted build: VEVYE 80%, IHEEZO 82%, TRIESENCE 80%, TYRVAYA 79% (company: branded-like before amort and inventory step-up), legacy/BYQLOVI 78%, compounding 55% (Q3 55.2%), G-MELT 72% after the Catalent comparator and manufacturing (S16), biosimilars 52% (S18). GAAP consolidated gross margin equals this product gross profit minus amortization, divided by revenue.

FY2027E core cash opex is the Q3 2026 cash run rate of $59.258 million, annualized and inflated 4% (S40, BLS ECI-based named rate), or $246.513 million. That run rate already includes the 2026 commercial expansion (Q3 SG&A $53.1 million vs. $35.9 million a year earlier) and elevated R&D (Q3 $10.3 million vs. $3.3 million) and already pays for the Q3 2026 revenue pace. TYRVAYA’s verified ~$20 million incremental annual opex is added once from FY2027E. Same-store volume-variable opex is 4% (S41) of same-store VEVYE, IHEEZO, TRIESENCE, legacy, compounding and other-revenue dollars above the Q3 2026 annualized same-store revenue (C17), so dedicated TYRVAYA, G-MELT and YOCHIL program costs and the Samsung take on BYOOVIZ/OPUVIZ are not double-counted as variable. Core opex then grows 4% a year. This is an assumption, not a company budget.

VEVYE volume through FY2032E holds the average reconstructed net add of 49,538.5 TRx per quarter. That is a transparent aggregate stock-flow proxy, not a prescriber, new-start, or refill cohort, and steady net additions are a judgment, not a finding of saturation. Percentage growth decelerates as the base rises (FY2027E TRx about 63% above FY2026E, then about 39%, 28%, 22%, 18%, and 15%). Q4 2026E derived net price of about $129.42 per TRx is held in FY2027E–FY2032E. A 1 January 2027 coverage win is real commentary and is not treated as a proven double-count of the Q4 exit; it is omitted from the base because covered-share and covered-versus-cash economics are not disclosed, and it is a bull-case increment of 8% above that exit, not a base-case rate. No later-year price increase is invented. TRx from Q3 2025 is reconstructed; revenue/TRx is derived, not a measured ASP. Composition-patent expiry from December 2030 is a later-window risk; other listed claims run into 2037–2039.

IHEEZO units use a constant annual add of 41,804 (the Q3 2026 year-over-year add of 10,665 divided by the 2025 Q3 seasonal weight) allocated with 2025 seasonal weights. The forward run-rate starts from a cleaned 2026 four-quarter rate of 243,849, which deseasonalizes Q3 2026 and does not carry Q2 2026 stocking into later years. FY2027E units are 285,654 and FY2028E 327,458, then the same add continues through FY2032E. FY2027E–FY2032E revenue is annual demand times the Q3 2026 realization of $406.64 per customer unit, with no net full-year inventory build (a recurring Q4 stock-in would need a Q1 reversal). Q4 2026E dollars alone include the 2024 recognition lift of 1.242. Realization is revenue per customer unit, not a true ASP.

TRIESENCE units hold the average net add of 5,044 customer units per quarter through FY2032E, from Q4 2026E 25,066 to FY2027E 150,704 and FY2028E 231,408. Realization is held at the Q3 2026 ratio of $534.76 per customer unit (not a true ASP). Percentage growth decelerates as the base rises. Steady net additions are a judgment, not a finding of saturation, and only two post-relaunch increments support the add. U.S. Orange Book patents are listed through 2029; they are a named bear lever and are not used to invent a base-case fade. The next-generation H-N08 pre-filled syringe is expected H2 2028 / H1 2029 but is unapproved and is not in the base as a replacement product.

Weighted product gross profit before amortization is the sum of line revenue × product GM rates in S19. GAAP gross margin = (product GP − amortization) / revenue. Adjusted EBITDA = product GP − cash opex, which equals GAAP GP + amortization add-back − cash opex.

FY2027E cash opex = 59.258×4×1.04 (core, S20/S40) + 20.0 (TYRVAYA) + 12.0 (G-MELT pre-launch) + 6.0 (YOCHIL program) + 4% (S41) of same-store revenue above the Q3 2026 annualized same-store revenue of 397.188 (C17). Later years: core grows 4%; TYRVAYA $20 continues; G-MELT program follows S17; YOCHIL program follows S33; variable is 4% of the same-store increment over that Q3 annualized base (VEVYE, IHEEZO, TRIESENCE, legacy, compounding, other revenues — not TYRVAYA, BYOOVIZ, OPUVIZ, BYQLOVI, G-MELT or YOCHIL). Before 12 November 2026 the increment was measured vs. FY2026E. Adjusted EBITDA = product gross profit before amortization − cash opex, i.e. revenue − cash cost.

FY2027E VEVYE $255 million and FY2028E $326 million are retained starting assumptions from the prior product build, not a user-chosen override of the rates. The $255 million applies 45% TRx growth to the full FY2026E year, not to a Q3-annualized starting point. Before the Q4 rounding used on the official line (51.133 to 51.1), FY2026E VEVYE is about $141.166 million. Reconstructed FY2026E TRx is 238,338 + 288,389 + 337,415 + (337,415 × 1.17) = 1,258,917.55. That implies a derived full-year net realization of about $112.13 per TRx and a Q4 exit realization of about $129.52 ($51.133 million / 394,775.55), so the Q4 exit is about 15.5% above the FY2026E average (129.52 / 112.13 ≈ 1.155). FY2027E then uses about 1,825,430 TRx (FY2026E TRx × 1.45) at about $139.89 per TRx (Q4 exit × 1.08), or 141.166 × 1.45 × 1.155 × 1.08 ≈ $255.3 million, rounded to the retained $255 million. The residual of about $0.3 million is rounding of that retained assumption, not an unexplained coverage plug. The 8% is the step-up from the Q4 exit; full-year FY2027E derived net price versus the FY2026E average is about 24.7%, not 8%. Revenue/TRx is a derived ratio, not a measured ASP, and TRx from Q3 2025 onward is reconstructed, not independently measured. FY2028E $326 million is not 255 × 1.25 × 1.02 = 325.125 rounded up. It equals $255 million × about 25.3% volume growth × 2% net price (326 / (255 × 1.02) − 1 = 25.336%). A plain 25% volume × 2% NPP on $255 million would be $325.1 million; the retained $326 million traces to an earlier rounded $255.5 million starting point in the prior build and is kept as approximately 25.3% volume and 2% NPP. FY2029E onward is a maturing franchise (about 18%, 14%, 12%, 10% revenue growth) with NPP roughly flat. Composition-patent expiry from December 2030 is a later-window risk; other listed claims run into 2037–2039. [Instance S21_1: value 326.0 tag S.]

FY2027E TRIESENCE $67.5 million and FY2028E $86.4 million are retained starting assumptions at a constant $535 realization (revenue per customer unit, not a true ASP). That implies about 126,200 units in FY2027E and about 161,500 units in FY2028E. FY2026E units are about 72,000 (9,934 + 14,603 + 20,022 + Q4 at the held +37.1% sequential rate). FY2027E is therefore a continued ramp year of about 75% unit growth from a still-low base, not a mature 21% grower, and FY2028E is about 28% unit growth. U.S. Orange Book patents are listed through 2029. The base lets units keep growing modestly into FY2029E (about 185,800 units, $99.4 million) then flatten in FY2030E–FY2031E and decline about 3% in FY2032E. The next-generation H-N08 pre-filled syringe is expected H2 2028 / H1 2029 but is unapproved and is not in the base as a replacement product. [Instance S23_1: value 86.4 tag S.]

The base uses 4%; the bear uses 8%.
